key_insight: A properly constructed first-order least-squares residual can reliably measure nonlinear PDE solution error in the equation’s natural norm near a solution branch.
engineering_relevance: For nonlinear solid mechanics, including compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, this supports surrogate training with an inference-time error indicator.
method: Establish residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Train a reduced-basis neural operator in a conforming finite element space, using solution snapshots only to construct the basis.
Assemble the physics loss and its symbolically derived gradient with a finite element library.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that square-root loss excess tracks error and that the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm when evaluated in the same finite element space.
watch_item: Guarantees depend on PDE-specific stability and regularity conditions and may hold only near a solution branch.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
